name: MyCareersFuture Guide: How to Find Jobs and Get Noticed in Singapore
content:
Key takeaways

  • MyCareersFuture (mycareersfuture.gov.sg) is a government job portal designed to match jobs to your skills, not only your search keywords, and to highlight roles that come with government support.
  • A complete profile — including an uploaded resume and accurately listed skills — significantly affects how well the platform matches you to relevant roles and how visible you are to employers.
  • You can set up job alerts so new matching postings come to you automatically, rather than manually checking the site every day.
  • The platform highlights jobs with government support, which can be particularly useful for career switchers.
  • Using MyCareersFuture well can meaningfully improve your job search, but it does not guarantee employment — outcomes still depend on your qualifications, how you present yourself, and market demand for your target role.

What makes MyCareersFuture different from commercial job boards

Unlike many private-sector job boards that match primarily on keywords in your search query versus a job title, MyCareersFuture is built around skills-based matching. The platform encourages both jobseekers and employers to list specific skills, and its matching engine tries to connect candidates to roles based on overlapping skills rather than relying purely on job title similarity.

This distinction matters most for career switchers — someone moving from, say, a retail management background into a logistics coordination role might not show up in a keyword search for "logistics coordinator," but could still be a strong match if their actual skills (inventory management, team coordination, scheduling) align with what the employer is looking for.

MyCareersFuture is also directly integrated into Singapore's broader workforce support ecosystem. It surfaces roles tied to structured government support — for example, positions connected to career conversion programmes or other Workforce Singapore-backed hiring initiatives — which can make employers more open to hiring candidates without traditional, direct experience in that exact role.

Step 1: Set up your account and complete your profile

Getting started requires logging in with Singpass, which creates your MyCareersFuture account if you're a new user. From there, a complete profile is the foundation of everything else the platform can do for you:

  1. Log in with Singpass.
  2. Click on your name in the top corner to open the account dropdown menu.
  3. Select Profile from the list of options.
  4. Fill in your employment history, education background, and any relevant certifications.

An incomplete profile — particularly one missing key employment history or education details — limits how effectively the platform can match you to relevant postings, and it also makes your profile less compelling to employers who browse candidate profiles directly.

Step 2: Upload your resume

Within your profile, there's a dedicated Resume section. Uploading a current, well-formatted resume here is essential, since:

  • Many employers will look at your uploaded resume directly when reviewing applications
  • An outdated or missing resume can significantly reduce your chances of being shortlisted, even if the rest of your profile is complete
  • Keeping this resume updated periodically — not just when you're actively job hunting — ensures you're always ready to apply quickly to a promising posting

Step 3: Add your skills to improve matching

One of MyCareersFuture's most underused features is the Add Skills function, which directly affects how the platform's matching engine treats your profile:

  1. Start a job search on MyCareersFuture using a role type or keyword relevant to your target career.
  2. Click the Add Skills button that appears alongside search results.
  3. Select skills that genuinely and accurately reflect your actual experience and capabilities.
  4. Log in with Singpass to save these skills permanently to your profile.

This step matters more than it might initially seem — accurately listed skills improve both how the platform surfaces relevant roles to you and how visible your profile is when employers search for candidates by specific skill sets, rather than by job title alone.

Step 4: Set up job alerts instead of manually checking

Rather than logging in daily to repeat the same searches, you can automate this process:

  1. Enter your target job title or relevant keywords into the search bar.
  2. Click Create Job Alert.
  3. New postings matching your specified criteria will be sent to you automatically going forward, without needing to manually search again.

This is particularly useful during an active job search, since popular postings can accumulate applications quickly, and being notified promptly gives you a better chance of applying while a posting is still fresh.

Step 5: Explore jobs with government support

MyCareersFuture specifically highlights postings connected to structured government-backed hiring or training initiatives:

  1. On the main page, look for and click Search jobs with government support.
  2. Browse through listings that come with associated support — this can include roles linked to career conversion programmes or other Workforce Singapore initiatives designed to help workers transition into new sectors.

These roles deserve particular attention if you're pivoting into an unfamiliar industry or role type, since the structured support attached to these positions (which can include training subsidies or incentives for the employer) often makes employers more willing to consider candidates who don't have direct prior experience in that exact role.

Step 6: Apply for jobs

Once your profile, resume, and skills are set up, applying is straightforward:

For new users:

  1. Click on your name to access account features and complete your Profile if you haven't already.
  2. Navigate to the Resume section and upload your resume.
  3. Search for a role of interest and click Apply.
  4. Follow the guided application steps presented by the platform.

For existing users with a completed profile:

  1. Log in to your account.
  2. Search for the role you're interested in.
  3. Click Apply.
  4. Follow the same guided steps to complete and submit your application.

Does applying through MyCareersFuture actually lead to interviews?

This is a fair and common question, and the honest answer is that results vary. Some jobseekers report genuinely securing interviews and even job offers directly from applications submitted through MyCareersFuture, which suggests that at least some employers and recruiters do actively review submissions through the platform rather than treating it purely as a passive listing board.

That said, as with virtually any job portal, response rates depend heavily on:

  • How closely your profile and skills match what the employer is actually looking for
  • The overall competitiveness of the specific role (popular roles attract more applicants)
  • How complete, current, and well-presented your profile and resume are
  • General hiring conditions in your target industry at that particular time

A generic, incomplete profile is unlikely to stand out regardless of which platform you use — the portal itself is a tool, not a guarantee of results.

Practical tips for better results on MyCareersFuture

  • Keep your resume genuinely current, updating it whenever you gain new experience, skills, or certifications, rather than only when you're actively searching.
  • Use accurate, specific skills rather than padding your profile with skills you don't actually have — mismatches can hurt your credibility if you're shortlisted and later interviewed.
  • Check job alerts promptly and apply as soon as reasonably possible after a relevant new posting appears, since popular listings can fill quickly.
  • Consider government-supported roles seriously if you're attempting a career pivot — the structured backing attached to these positions can genuinely improve your odds compared to applying for the same type of role without that support.
  • Tailor your profile summary and resume where the platform allows, rather than relying on a single generic version for every application.

How career switchers specifically can use MyCareersFuture

If you're trying to move into a new industry or role type, MyCareersFuture offers a few specific advantages worth leaning into:

  • Skills-based matching means your profile can surface for roles you might not have found through a straightforward job-title search.
  • Government-supported job filters can highlight roles specifically designed to bring in career switchers, often with training support built into the hiring arrangement.
  • The Add Skills function lets you proactively signal transferable skills from your previous industry, which might not be obvious from your job title alone.

Combining these features — a complete profile, accurately listed transferable skills, and a focus on government-supported postings — gives career switchers a more realistic path into a new field than simply applying to postings that match their previous job title.

Frequently asked questions

Is MyCareersFuture free to use? Yes, it's a free government platform for jobseekers, developed and run by Workforce Singapore.

Do I need Singpass to use MyCareersFuture? Yes, Singpass is required to log in and to save your profile, skills, resume, and job alerts to your account.

How do I improve my chances of being noticed by employers? Complete your profile fully, upload a current and accurate resume, and add skills that genuinely reflect your capabilities — these factors directly affect both how the platform matches you to relevant roles and how visible you are when employers search for candidates.

What does "jobs with government support" mean? These are job postings connected to structured government-backed initiatives, such as career conversion or training-linked hiring support, which can be especially useful if you're switching industries or roles.

Can I set up alerts for more than one type of job? Yes, you can create multiple job alerts for different search terms or job titles, allowing you to cover a broader range of roles you might be interested in.

Does using MyCareersFuture guarantee I'll get a job? No. MyCareersFuture is a tool that can improve your visibility and matching to relevant roles, but actual hiring outcomes still depend on your qualifications, how competitive the specific role is, and broader market conditions — no job portal can guarantee employment.

Final practical takeaway

MyCareersFuture works best when treated as more than a simple listings page. Completing your profile fully, uploading and maintaining a current resume, adding accurate skills, and setting up job alerts all directly affect your visibility and match quality on the platform — and for career switchers in particular, the skills-matching approach and government-supported job filters can open doors that a straightforward job-title search would miss.
